# v0.49.50

This patch adds an output-width option for embedding models that support it, stops background runs from retrying a model whose provider said when to come back, and fixes a wrong context-size reading after an Anthropic server-side fallback on OpenCode 2.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Added

- **`embedding.dimensions` (issue 405):** an optional output width for OpenAI-compatible embedding models that can return shorter vectors, such as OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-*` and Qwen3-Embedding. Set it to an integer from 1 to 8192 in your user config, and Magic Context sends it as the `dimensions` field of each embedding request. Leave it unset and nothing changes: the request omits the field, and your stored vectors stay valid. Setting or changing it re-embeds your memories and history at the new width, because vectors of different widths can't be compared. Magic Context refuses a response whose width differs from the one you asked for. A project config can't set this option; it is read from your user config only. Thanks to @yiyi-wei for the contribution.

## Fixed

- **Background runs no longer retry a model that is out of quota:** when the summarizer or the dreamer has `fallback_models` and a provider refuses the first model with a time to retry after (a used-up quota window, for example), every later run used to try that model again first, fail, and fall back. Each run left one failed child session and, on OpenCode, an error box in the parent session's terminal. Later background runs now skip that model until the time the provider gave and start on the next one in your list. Your configured order returns after that time, and a successful run on the model clears it at once. When every model in the list is waiting, Magic Context still tries the one that frees soonest. A restart clears this memory, and your own session's requests are never rerouted. It works on OpenCode 1 and on OpenCode 2.2 or newer. Pi and older OpenCode 2 versions don't pass the provider's retry time to plugins, so runs there fall back as before.
- **Context size after an Anthropic server-side fallback on OpenCode 2 (issue 877):** when Anthropic refuses a request on one model and answers it on its fallback model, the reported usage is the sum of both attempts. Magic Context read that sum as the size of the prompt, so one fallback step could look like 110% of the window. The session then held turns, refused them, or summarized early. With the CortexKit anthropic-auth plugin, which records each attempt's usage, Magic Context now takes the size of the attempt that produced the reply. When that record is missing or unreadable, it keeps the previous reading instead of the summed one. Thanks to @iceteaSA for the report and the fix.

# v0.49.49

This patch stops sessions near their context limit from rewriting the prompt for tiny summaries, and keeps Magic Context's per-project working files out of `git status`.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **No more tiny summaries near the limit (issue 886):** once a session reached the near-limit band, Magic Context summarized any history that had just left the recent tail, often one or two steps. Each of those summaries changed the cached prompt, so a session sitting in that band rewrote its whole prompt every few steps. A minimum size that should have prevented this never applied. Near the limit, a summary now waits until the history it covers holds at least 2% of the usable window, counting text and tool inputs (tool outputs leave the prompt by other means). Manual `/ctx-wrapup` and `/ctx-recomp`, usage at or above 95%, overflow recovery, and the recovery after switching to a model with a smaller window still summarize whatever is ready, so they never wait. Below the near-limit band nothing changes.
- **Working files no longer show in `git status` (issue 891):** Magic Context wrote its ignore rule into the shared `.cortexkit/.gitignore`, which itself showed up as an untracked file, so `git status` listed `.cortexkit/` after the first summary. Magic Context now writes `.cortexkit/magic-context/.gitignore` containing `*` whenever it creates that folder, for summarizer dumps and documentation proposals alike. It removes its own old entry from the shared file, leaves other tools' entries untouched, and deletes the shared file only if nothing else is left in it. `.cortexkit/magic-context.jsonc` stays trackable. `setup` no longer edits your repository's root `.gitignore`; lines it added before can stay.

# v0.49.48

This patch stops OpenCode sessions from replaying an outdated todo list when the agent uses a custom todo status.

## Upgrading

Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Todo lists with custom statuses are kept (issue 892):** OpenCode's `todowrite` accepts any status or priority text, such as `blocked`, but Magic Context only recognised the four built-in statuses and three priorities. It ignored any other list, so it kept the older list and showed it to the agent as its latest plan whenever the prompt was rebuilt. Magic Context now keeps every list the way OpenCode stores it, and treats every status other than `completed` and `cancelled` as still open. A list it can't read at all clears its saved copy instead of leaving an old one in place. Lists that only use the built-in values are stored exactly as before. Pi is unchanged, because its `todowrite` tool already refuses other values.

# v0.49.47

This patch keeps Claude's kept reasoning valid when a session's tool list changes, makes a manual `/compact` on OpenCode 2 land queued cleanup in the rebuild it already causes, and reads assistant replies that OpenCode 2.2.6 stores in its new parts table.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.
- OpenCode 2.2.6 sessions that already store assistant replies in the parts table rebuild their history once after this update. Other sessions are unaffected.

## Fixed

- **Kept reasoning survives a tool list change:** on Claude Fable 5.1 and 5.2, Mythos, and the 5.5 models, a thinking block stays valid only while everything sent before it is unchanged, including the list of tools. When a tool was added, removed or edited mid-session (an MCP server connecting, for example), the next request still carried thinking bound to the old list, and Fable 5.2 and Mythos rejected it with a 400 error. On OpenCode 2 and Pi, Magic Context now notices the change and removes the affected thinking on that turn, together with any cleanup it was waiting to do, since that turn rewrites the prompt anyway. OpenCode 2 also recovers on the next turn after such a rejection, which it didn't before. OpenCode 1 can't see each request's tools, so it keeps recovering after one rejected request.
- **A manual `/compact` on OpenCode 2 carries the queued cleanup:** a manual compaction rebuilds the start of the prompt, so the provider's cache is lost on the next request anyway. Magic Context now removes the content the agent already marked as no longer needed, and does its routine cleanup, on that request instead of waiting for a second rebuild. If the turn was holding recent reasoning, that reasoning is removed with the old history rather than sent behind the new one, which the provider would reject. This also works when the session was reopened just before `/compact`.
- **OpenCode 2.2.6 replies stored in the parts table are read:** OpenCode 2.2.6 can store assistant replies in a separate parts table, with `experimental.part_rows`, and for some replies it inserts complete. Magic Context didn't read that table. So once OpenCode 2 compacted the session (a manual `/compact`, or the checkpoint Magic Context adds to keep long sessions fast), every earlier assistant reply was missing from the request, and summaries saw no assistant text. It now reads the table exactly as OpenCode does.

# v0.49.46

This patch fixes two OpenCode 2 problems that kept sessions large and expensive: tool catalogs piling up when MCP servers connect and disconnect, and oversized requests after switching to a model with a smaller context window. OpenCode 2 checkpoints also show a short note instead of the full history.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.
- On OpenCode 2, avoid going back to 0.49.45 or earlier after this version has written a checkpoint. Older versions read the new checkpoint note as the summary of earlier history in subagent sessions.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 no longer piles up tool catalogs from MCP servers:** each time an MCP server connected or disconnected, OpenCode 2 added a new copy of the tool catalog to the conversation, and Magic Context removed old copies only when a newer one restated every server at once. MCP changes arrive one server at a time, so old copies were almost never removed, and a long session could carry hundreds of them. Magic Context now removes a copy once every server it mentions has a newer entry, including copies already covered by the history summary. Removal happens only on a turn that already rebuilds the prompt. In a test run that toggled an MCP server every few turns, the request went from 39 catalog copies to 1, and prompt rewrites from 30 to 6. Thanks to @dhaern for the detailed report (#886).
- **Context usage is measured against the right window when the provider reports no usage:** in that case Magic Context counts the request itself. It divided by the wrong window size, which made usage look 20–30% lower than it was, and its 95% safety lines ignored a model's input limit. Both now use the window the provider's own readings use, capped by the input limit (#886).
- **Switching to a model with a smaller context window no longer sends oversized requests:** after switching, for example, from a 1M-token model to a 200k one, Magic Context summarized one chunk of history per turn and sent each request anyway, so the provider rejected turn after turn. It now keeps summarizing within the same turn until the request fits. If it still can't fit, it refuses the turn with a clear message instead of sending a request that would fail. The next turn continues. In a real OpenCode 2 run, the switch took one turn instead of nine failed ones. Thanks to @dragon-Elec for the report (#889).
- **OpenCode 2 checkpoints show a short note:** when Magic Context adds a checkpoint to keep an OpenCode 2 session fast, the conversation showed the whole history summary, memories included, under a "Compaction" divider. It now shows a one-line note saying the history is unchanged. The model still receives the same history as before (#889).
- **`doctor --issue` keeps the wording of log lines:** issue reports replaced the text of almost every log line with `<text omitted>`, which left them hard to read. The fixed wording of Magic Context's own log lines is now kept, and only the values inserted into them are judged one by one: numbers, durations and model names are kept, paths and ids are replaced with aliases, and anything else is left out.
- **`ctx_memory` argument descriptions name the placeholders:** some hosts require every argument. The descriptions now say to pass an empty list for `ids` when writing, and empty text for `content` when archiving or reading.
